topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecture opens with framing remarks on the course structure, the impact of cancer, and the session's learning outcomes.

topics.label: Biological mechanisms and tissue architecture in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore cancer as a failure of cellular differentiation and three-dimensional tissue organization driven by genetic, epigenetic, and viral factors.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and the benign-to-malignant transition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the pathological processes of local invasion and metastatic spread that distinguish malignant cancers from benign tumors using clinical specimens and colorectal histology.

topics.label: Clinical behavior, nomenclature, and mechanisms of tumor morbidity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the pathological naming conventions, progression potential, and physiological mechanisms through which tumors cause disease and death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence and comparative oncology across species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics present epidemiological incidence and mortality data for human cancers alongside tumor patterns observed in companion animals and other multicellular taxa.

topics.label: Clinical presentation and cancer screening strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the presenting symptoms of tumors and evaluate population screening methods across cervical, colorectal, breast, and prostate cancers.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practicals preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecture closes with final administrative remarks reviewing the learning outcomes and pointing forward to the upcoming practical sessions.
